chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “It is appropriate for the menstruating woman to perform wudu (ablution) at the time of every salat (prayer), then face the qiblah and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the amount of time she would normally pray.”

key_terms.فَتَذْكُرَ اللَّهَ: then she remembers Allah through dhikr
key_terms.مِقْدَارَ مَا كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي: for the length of time she would normally perform the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a menstruating woman do at the time of each salat (prayer) according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal and devotional instruction concerning a menstruating woman during the times of salat (prayer). Although she does not perform the salat itself, she is encouraged to maintain a state of devotional remembrance by performing wudu (ablution), facing the qiblah, and engaging in dhikr for the duration of the prayer.
